questions.explanation: p.22 lists increased transaction volumes, greater numbers of users, more connections, and more locations. Zero downtime is a resilience/availability concern, not a scalability capacity example.
questions.source: p.22: 'Increased transaction volumes / Greater numbers of users / More connections / More locations'

questions.question: Which scaling approach uses an even more powerful server?
options: Vertical scaling
Horizontal scaling
Static load balancing
Federated geographic distribution
questions.explanation: p.23 shows Vertical Scaling as Server to More Powerful Server to Even More Powerful Server. Horizontal Scaling adds additional servers.
questions.source: p.23: 'Vertical Scaling / More Powerful Server / Even More Powerful Server'

questions.question: Which scaling approach adds additional servers?
options: Horizontal scaling
Vertical scaling
Active-passive resilience
System of record reconciliation
questions.explanation: p.23 shows Horizontal Scaling as Server plus Additional Server, Additional Server, Additional Server. Vertical scaling upgrades to a more powerful server.
questions.source: p.23: 'Horizontal Scaling / Additional Server / Additional Server'

questions.question: How do the slides define throughput as a performance requirement?
options: Transactions per time period
Time to complete a transaction
A variance threshold such as 90% under 100 milliseconds
The number of servers in a data center
questions.explanation: p.24 defines throughput as transactions per time period. Latency is time to complete a transaction. A variance threshold is a way performance can be measured.
questions.source: p.24: 'Throughput: transactions per time period'

questions.question: How do the slides define latency as a performance requirement?
options: Time to complete a transaction
Transactions per time period
The number of active-passive servers
The number of users in a branch
questions.explanation: p.24 defines latency as time to complete a transaction. Throughput is transactions per time period.
questions.source: p.24: 'Latency: time to complete a transaction'

questions.question: The slides state that performance can be measured as average, maximum allowable, or a variance threshold such as 90% under 100 milliseconds.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.24 says performance can be measured as Average, Maximum allowable, and A variance threshold (e.g. 90% under 100 milliseconds). The statement matches.
questions.source: p.24: 'Average / Maximum allowable / A variance threshold (e.g. 90% under 100 milliseconds)'

questions.question: The slides state that poor performance is a common issue for many solution deliveries and should be considered in all stages of the development lifecycle.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.24 explicitly says poor performance is a common issue for many solution deliveries and should be considered in all stages of the development lifecycle.
questions.source: p.24: 'Poor performance is a common issue / Should be considered in all stages of the development lifecycle'

questions.question: The slides list marking data records as deleted rather than actually deleting them as a common auditability and data integrity approach.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.26 lists marking data records as deleted rather than actually deleting them as one common approach for maintaining an unalterable record. The statement is correct.
questions.source: p.26: 'Marking data records as deleted rather than actually deleting them'

questions.question: What is a 'system of record' according to the slides?
options: A designated master source for specific types of information
A load balancer that routes service requests
A blockchain node that mines new blocks
A diagram showing servers and network hardware
questions.explanation: p.26 defines a system of record as designated as the master source for specific types of information. It is used with reconciliation to ensure intersystem data consistency and integrity.
questions.source: p.26: 'Identifying a system of record that is designated as the master source for specific types of information'

questions.question: How do the slides define adaptability and maintainability?
options: A solution's ability to be changed and supported after it has been deployed
A solution's ability to process transactions per time period
A solution's ability to hide all details from business users
A solution's ability to eliminate all future technological change
questions.explanation: p.27 defines adaptability and maintainability as a solution's ability to be changed and supported after it has been deployed. Business and technological evolution necessitates change.
questions.source: p.27: 'Solutions ability to be changed and supported after they have been deployed'

questions.question: What lifecycle sequence is shown on p.27?
options: Develop, Use, Refine, Retire
Develop, Retire, Use, Refine
Use, Develop, Retire, Refine
Refine, Develop, Use, Retire
questions.explanation: p.27 shows Develop, Use, Refine, Retire, with a loop from Refine back to Use. The other sequences do not match the diagram.
questions.source: p.27: diagram 'Develop / Use / Refine / Retire'

questions.question: Which statement correctly matches geographic distribution approaches in the slides?
options: Centralized: processing or data managed at a central location; Federated: some functions central and others delegated; Distributed: localities have full autonomy
Centralized: localities have full autonomy; Federated: no central management; Distributed: one central location
Centralized: load balancer chooses all requests; Federated: static symbol ranges; Distributed: round robin
Centralized: blockchain nodes; Federated: smart contracts; Distributed: proof-of-stake
questions.explanation: p.28 defines centralized as processing or data managed and maintained at a central location, federated as some functions managed centrally while others delegated to regional/local implementation, and distributed as localities having full autonomy.
questions.source: p.28: 'Centralized / Federated / Distributed / Localities have full autonomy'

questions.question: Which statement describes static load balancing according to the slides?
options: It segregates distribution requirements across a predefined set of components and is simple to implement but has suboptimal load allocation
It uses a load balancer to decide which source receives each request based on availability
It requires bidirectional communication and a round-robin algorithm
It provides full autonomy to every locality
questions.explanation: p.30 defines static load balancing as segregating distribution requirements across a predefined set of components, using symbol name ranges to define service separation; it is simple but suboptimal. Options B and C describe dynamic load balancing.
questions.source: p.30: 'Segregate the distribution requirements across a predefined set of components / Simple to implement / Suboptimal allocation of load'

questions.question: In the static load balancing diagram on p.31, a service request with symbol TAV is routed to which Distribution Manager?
options: Distribution Manager (S-Z)
Distribution Manager (A-G)
Distribution Manager (H-R)
The Load Balancer
questions.explanation: p.31 shows Service Request (Symbol = TAV) pointing to Distribution Manager (S-Z), because TAV falls in the S-Z symbol range. A-G and H-R cover other ranges; there is no Load Balancer in the static diagram.
questions.source: p.31: diagram 'Service Request (Symbol = TAV)' to 'Distribution Manager (S-Z)'

questions.question: Which statements about dynamic load balancing are correct according to the slides?
options: A load balancer component intermediates service requests and decides which source to route to
It requires bidirectional communication and a load allocation algorithm such as round robin
It may factor in the status or availability of service sources
It is simpler to implement than static load balancing
questions.explanation: p.32 says dynamic load balancing uses a load balancer to intermediate requests and decide routing; it is more complex, requires bidirectional communication and a load allocation algorithm such as round robin, and may factor in status/availability. It is more complex, not simpler, than static.
questions.source: p.32: 'A load balancer component intermediates service requests / Requires bidirectional communication / round robin / May factor in status/availability'

questions.question: In the dynamic load balancing diagram on p.33, what is the role of the Load Balancer?
options: It intermediates the service request and routes it to one of the feed handlers
It stores the permanent ledger of all transactions
It defines symbol name ranges for static separation
It acts as the system of record for customer data
questions.explanation: p.33 shows the Subscribing Application sending a Service Request to the Load Balancer, which routes to Feed Handler #1, #2, ... #N. It does not store a ledger, define static ranges, or act as a system of record.
questions.source: p.33: diagram 'Service Request' to 'Load Balancer' to 'Feed Handler #1/#2/#N'

questions.question: The slides state that monolithic applications tightly couple frontend, backend, and database components and use a single codebase with one language and platform.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.34 defines monolithic applications as tightly coupling frontend, backend, and database components, with a single codebase using one language and platform. The statement matches.
questions.source: p.34: 'Monolithic applications tightly couple frontend, backend, and database components / A single codebase uses one language and platform'

questions.question: What does the slides say about updates in a monolithic architecture?
options: Entire application redeployment is required, leading to infrequent updates
Each small function can be deployed independently without redeploying the application
Updates never require compatibility checks
Only the database component is redeployed
questions.explanation: p.34 says tight coupling complicates maintenance, updates, and scalability of individual components, and entire application redeployment is required, leading to infrequent updates. Independent deployment is a microservices trait.
questions.source: p.34: 'Entire application redeployment is required, leading to infrequent updates'

questions.question: Which microservice type operates CRUD functions, scales horizontally, and is standalone?
options: Atomic services
Wrapper services
Composite services
Static distribution managers
questions.explanation: p.35 says atomic services operate CRUD functions, scale horizontally, and are standalone. Wrapper services expose monolithic functionality but rely on other applications; composite services orchestrate multiple services.
questions.source: p.35: 'Atomic services operate CRUD functions, scale horizontally, and are standalone'

questions.question: Which service types are described in the microservices architecture model on p.35?
options: Atomic services
Wrapper services
Composite services
Distribution Manager services
questions.explanation: p.35 describes atomic, wrapper, and composite services. Distribution Manager is from static load balancing diagrams, not the microservices model.
questions.source: p.35: 'Atomic services / Wrapper services / Composite services'

questions.question: What trade-off of SOA microservices is mentioned in the slides?
options: They offer flexibility, scalability, and reuse but add overhead and latency
They eliminate all latency and overhead
They prevent independent deployment of small functions
They require a single codebase and one platform
questions.explanation: p.35 says SOA microservices offer flexibility, scalability, and reuse but add overhead and latency. The other options contradict the slide or describe monolithic architecture.
questions.source: p.35: 'SOA microservices offer flexibility, scalability, and reuse but adds overhead and latency'

questions.question: Which functions do API gateways provide for enterprise applications according to the slides?
options: Managing service access, load balancing, version control, caching, logging, and monitoring
Mining new blockchain blocks and reaching consensus
Holding smart contract value in escrow
Defining proof-of-stake rewards
questions.explanation: p.36 says API gateways manage service access, load balancing, and version control, and provide caching, logging, and monitoring. Blockchain mining, escrow, and proof-of-stake are DLT concepts.
questions.source: p.36: 'API gateways manage service access, load balancing, and version control / caching, logging, and monitoring'

questions.question: Which are drawbacks of API gateways listed in the slides?
options: Added latency
Complexity
Maintenance needs
Guaranteed elimination of all security risks
questions.explanation: p.36 lists drawbacks of API gateways as added latency, complexity, and maintenance needs. It does not claim they eliminate all security risks.
questions.source: p.36: 'Drawbacks of API gateways include added latency, complexity, and maintenance needs'

questions.question: Which statement describes publish-subscribe communications in the slides?
options: They support event-driven, real-time, asynchronous communication
They require a single monolithic codebase
They use only static symbol ranges to route requests
They eliminate the need for message-oriented middleware
questions.explanation: p.37 says publish-subscribe messaging supports event-driven, real-time, asynchronous communication. Message-oriented middleware enables event publishing and subscription handling. Other options are unrelated or contradictory.
questions.source: p.37: 'Publish-subscribe messaging supports event-driven, real-time, asynchronous communication'

questions.question: The slides state that AMQP enables interoperable publish-subscribe communication with brokers.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.37 says AMQP enables interoperable publish-subscribe communication with brokers. Message queuing ensures delivery; MOM enables event publishing and subscription handling.
questions.source: p.37: 'AMQP enables interoperable publish-subscribe communication with brokers'

questions.question: In the MOM-based system integration diagram on p.38, what sits inside the Message-oriented Middleware box?
options: Process Orchestration
A Load Balancer
A Blockchain Node
A System of Record
questions.explanation: p.38 shows Message-oriented Middleware containing Process Orchestration. Adapters connect source systems to the middleware, which handles communication, routing, filtering, transformation, connectivity, and transformation.
questions.source: p.38: diagram 'Message-oriented Middleware' containing 'Process Orchestration'

questions.question: What does the slides say about API granularity?
options: Granularity in APIs affects performance
Granularity has no effect on performance
Granularity only affects legal contracts
Granularity eliminates the need for API gateways
questions.explanation: p.39 says API design requires careful selection of exposed methods and granularity in APIs affects performance. It does not say granularity has no effect or eliminates API gateways.
questions.source: p.39: 'Granularity in APIs affects performance'

questions.question: Which statements about API design considerations are correct according to the slides?
options: Wrapper APIs ease integration but require updates if underlying systems change
Generic service APIs offer reusability but need significant planning and effort
Balancing flexibility, security, and maintenance is key
API design should ignore exposed methods and granularity
questions.explanation: p.39 says wrapper APIs ease integration but require updates if underlying systems change; generic APIs offer reusability but need planning/effort; balancing flexibility, security, and maintenance is key. It also says API design requires careful selection of exposed methods and granularity matters, so D is wrong.
questions.source: p.39: 'Wrapper APIs ease integration but require updates / Generic service APIs offer reusability / Balancing flexibility, security, and maintenance is key'

questions.question: Which factors affect cloud usage according to the slides?
options: Enterprise cloud computing strategy
Purpose and users of the solution
Dependencies on other internal systems
Type of information to be stored in the cloud, such as account and/or personally identifiable information
questions.explanation: p.40 lists enterprise cloud strategy, purpose/users, dependencies on internal systems, off-the-shelf resources internal or cloud, and type of information such as account/PII. All four options reflect listed factors.
questions.source: p.40: 'Enterprise cloud computing strategy / Purpose and users / Dependencies on other internal systems / Type of information'

questions.question: How do the slides compare fintech companies and financial institutions regarding cloud services?
options: Fintech companies typically can leverage cloud services with minimal complications, while financial institutions often face more challenges such as vendor management and internal policies
Financial institutions always have no cloud challenges, while fintech companies face all regulatory barriers
Both always face identical challenges with no differences
Only financial institutions are allowed to use cloud services
questions.explanation: p.41 says fintech companies typically can leverage cloud services with minimal complications, while financial institutions often face more challenges such as vendor management processes and internal policies/guidelines.
questions.source: p.41: 'Fintech companies typically can leverage cloud services with minimal complications / Financial institutions often face more challenges'

questions.question: Why does the slides say it is important to have an enterprise-level cloud strategy?
options: To provide guidance on when and how cloud services should be utilized
To guarantee every solution is deployed in the public cloud
To eliminate vendor management processes
To replace all internal systems immediately
questions.explanation: p.41 says it is important to have an enterprise-level cloud strategy to provide guidance on when and how cloud services should be utilized. It does not guarantee public cloud or eliminate vendor management.
questions.source: p.41: 'Important to have an enterprise-level cloud strategy to provide guidance on when and how cloud services should be utilized'

questions.question: How do the slides define a distributed ledger?
options: It keeps track of ownership and transaction flows between participants and is not managed and maintained by a central authority
It is a permanent record managed only by a central bank
It is a static load balancing table based on symbol ranges
It is a physical diagram of servers and network hardware
questions.explanation: p.42 defines a distributed ledger as keeping track of ownership and transaction flows between participants and not managed/maintained by a central authority; multiple parties perform recordkeeping/updating on copies in parallel.
questions.source: p.42: 'Keeps track of ownership and transaction flows between participants / Not managed and maintained by a central authority'

questions.question: The slides describe a distributed ledger as maintained by multiple parties that perform recordkeeping and updating activities on copies of the ledger in parallel, and as a type of distributed database.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.42 says the distributed ledger is maintained by multiple parties performing recordkeeping and updating on copies in parallel and is a type of distributed database. The statement matches.
questions.source: p.42: 'Maintained by multiple parties / Copies of the ledger in parallel / A type of distributed database'

questions.question: Which properties does the slides associate with distributed ledger data structure and management in some applications?
options: Permanent record
Immutable
Transparent
Secure
questions.explanation: p.43 says the data structure and management process typically provides a permanent record that is immutable, transparent, and secure. Cryptography is commonly used to secure information and authenticate parties.
questions.source: p.43: 'Permanent record that is immutable, transparent, and secure'

questions.question: Which are key components of the Bitcoin blockchain structure and mechanics described in the slides?
options: A network protocol that supports communication between participants
A network of computers that store and manage transaction data
A process for managing records based on achieving consensus between participants
A central authority that owns and maintains the ledger
questions.explanation: p.44 lists a network protocol, a network of computers storing/managing transaction data, and a consensus-based record management process. It also says distributed ledgers are not managed by a central authority, so D is wrong.
questions.source: p.44: 'A network protocol / A network of computers / A process for managing records based on achieving consensus'

questions.question: What is a permissionless blockchain implementation according to the slides?
options: It allows open access to the distributed ledger
It limits who can participate in the network
It requires a central authority to approve all records
It uses static symbol ranges to route requests
questions.explanation: p.44 says permissionless blockchain implementations allow open access to the distributed ledger. Permissioned implementations limit who can participate.
questions.source: p.44: 'Permissionless blockchain implementations allow open access to the distributed ledger'

questions.question: What is a permissioned blockchain implementation according to the slides?
options: It limits who can participate in the network
It allows anyone open access to the ledger
It eliminates the need for consensus
It requires no nodes
questions.explanation: p.44 says permissioned blockchain implementations limit who can participate in the network. Permissionless implementations allow open access.
questions.source: p.44: 'Permissioned blockchain implementations limit who can participate in the network'

questions.question: In the blockchain processing sequence, what do nodes validate before a transaction is grouped into a block?
options: The transaction's digital signature and previous recorded transactions to verify that the address transferring funds actually owns them
The exact physical location of every miner node
The enterprise cloud strategy
The API gateway's version control policy
questions.explanation: p.45 says nodes validate the transaction's digital signature and review previous transactions recorded by the blockchain to verify that the address transferring funds actually owns them. Other options are unrelated.
questions.source: p.45: 'Nodes validate the transaction's digital signature and review previous transactions ... verify that the address transferring the funds actually owns them'

questions.question: What do miner nodes do in the blockchain processing sequence according to the slides?
options: Perform computationally intensive verification of the block
Manage the enterprise service bus
Define HTML5 presentation standards
Route service requests using round robin
questions.explanation: p.45 says miner nodes perform computationally intensive verification of the block; when they reach consensus that transaction information is valid, the transaction is approved for inclusion in the ledger.
questions.source: p.45: 'Miner nodes will perform computationally intensive verification of the block'

questions.question: Which statements about blockchain consensus, rewards, and hash functions are correct according to the slides?
options: Nodes that contribute computing resources to validate transactions are rewarded with a small amount of the underlying digital currency
Two consensus mechanisms used are proof-of-work and proof-of-stake
Cryptographic hash functions are used to prevent tampering with transaction details
The consensus mechanism encourages bad actors to enter false information
questions.explanation: p.46 says nodes contributing computing resources are rewarded with digital currency; proof-of-work and proof-of-stake are used; cryptographic hash functions prevent tampering. It says consensus helps prevent fraudulent activity by bad actors, so D is wrong.
questions.source: p.46: 'Rewarded with a small amount of its underlying digital currency / Proof-of-work Proof-of-stake / Cryptographic hash functions ... prevent tampering'

questions.question: The slides list decentralized, trust in the design of the system, immutability, and fully automated as special characteristics of DLT.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.47 lists Decentralized, Trust, Immutability, and Fully automated as special characteristics. Decentralized means no owner and no single point of failure; trust is in design, not central authority.
questions.source: p.47: 'Decentralized / Trust / Immutability / Fully automated'

questions.question: How do the slides describe smart contracts?
options: Computer programs that can execute the terms of an agreement between users of the blockchain network
Static load balancing tables based on symbol ranges
Physical diagrams of servers and network hardware
A system of record for customer information
questions.explanation: p.48 describes smart contracts as an offshoot of blockchain technology: computer programs that can execute the terms of an agreement between users of the blockchain network.
questions.source: p.48: 'Computer programs that can execute the terms of an agreement between users of the blockchain network'

questions.question: Which benefits of smart contracts are listed in the slides?
options: Faster
Lower cost
Reduced risk of errors
Guaranteed legal enforceability in every jurisdiction
questions.explanation: p.48 lists benefits as faster, lower cost, and reduced risk of errors. It does not claim guaranteed legal enforceability in every jurisdiction; p.49 instead notes legal/regulatory frameworks may need alteration.
questions.source: p.48: 'Benefits: faster, lower cost, reduced risk of errors'

questions.question: For which situations does the slides say DLT is a good fit?
options: Multiple writers of information to a shared repository
Eliminating the need for intermediaries in a transaction process
Geographically distributed participants
A single writer using a standalone spreadsheet with no shared repository
questions.explanation: p.49 lists multiple writers to a shared repository, eliminating intermediaries, and geographically distributed participants as good fits. A single writer with no shared repository is not listed.
questions.source: p.49: 'Multiple writers of information to a shared repository / Eliminating the need for intermediaries / Geographically distributed participants'

questions.question: The slides identify the need to replace infrastructure, significant changes to existing processes, and alterations to legal or regulatory frameworks as nontechnical implementation requirements that could hinder DLT.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.49 says nontechnical implementation requirements that could be hinderances also need to be considered, including the need to replace infrastructure, significant changes to existing processes, and alterations to legal or regulatory frameworks.
questions.source: p.49: 'The need to replace infrastructure / Significant changes to existing processes / Alterations to legal or regulatory frameworks'

questions.question: Which are DLT application examples listed in the slides?
options: Digital currencies and payments
Trade finance
Property title registry
Syndicated loans and settlement of securities
questions.explanation: p.50 lists digital currencies, payments, trade finance, property title registry, syndicated loans, and settlement of securities as DLT application examples. All four options reflect listed examples.
questions.source: p.50: 'Digital currencies / Payments / Trade finance / Property title registry / Syndicated loans / Settlement of securities'

questions.question: Which challenges of DLT are listed in the slides?
options: Competing standards and unclear which platforms will be viable long term
Privacy and security flaws that could undermine applications
Regulatory and legal uncertainty, especially for heavily regulated entities such as banks
Guaranteed permanent support for every platform
questions.explanation: p.51 lists competing standards, privacy/security concerns, and regulatory/legal uncertainty especially for banks. It says it is unclear which platforms will be viable long term, so D is wrong.
questions.source: p.51: 'Competing standards / Privacy and security / Regulatory and legal uncertainty'

questions.question: According to the slides, whether IT is a commodity or a strategic asset for a financial institution depends mainly on what?
options: The institution and where its strategic advantage comes from
Whether the bank uses waterfall or code and fix for every project
The number of pages in the requirements document
Whether all vendors are local rather than remote
questions.explanation: p.2 指出 IT 是 commodity（商品）还是 strategic asset（战略资产）取决于 institution（机构）以及其 strategic advantage（战略优势）来自哪里。waterfall（瀑布式）、code and fix（编码并修复）是交付方式；文档页数和供应商地点不是该页判断依据。
questions.source: p.2: 'Depends on the institution and where its strategic advantage comes from'

questions.question: The slides state that in both cases it is critical to ensure that the expected return on IT solution investments is achieved.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.2 在讨论有些机构增加 technology investment（技术投资）未必带来 material benefits（实质性收益）、有些机构则依赖技术投资决定 relative success（相对成功）之后，明确说 in both cases it is critical to ensure that the expected return on IT solution investments（IT 解决方案投资的预期回报）is achieved。因此该判断正确。
questions.source: p.2: 'expected return on IT solution investments is achieved'

questions.question: Which example do the slides use to illustrate how quickly a technology firm can roll out changes to its production software environment?
options: Amazon rolls out changes to its production software environment several times a minute
Google uses only annual releases for all software
Uber replaces its entire codebase only after a waterfall review
A bank uses code and fix for every core banking release
questions.explanation: p.3 明确说 Amazon is able to roll out changes to their production software environment several times a minute（每分钟多次向生产软件环境发布变更）。Google 和 Uber 在 slides 中是用来说明 technology can be used to create and upset entire industries（创造并颠覆整个行业），不是每年发布或瀑布评审。
questions.source: p.3: 'Amazon is able to roll out changes to their production software environment several times a minute'

questions.question: Which question is listed in the agile software development case study on p.4?
options: What types of banking applications would be best suited for agile development?
How many ATMs are located in each branch?
Which bank has the largest market capitalization?
How can all vendors be eliminated from solution delivery?
questions.explanation: p.4 的 case study 问题包括哪些 banking applications（银行应用）最适合 agile development（敏捷开发）、sprints（短迭代）的好处、对 stakeholders（利益相关者）的影响、以及 agile 相比 waterfall model（瀑布模型）如何更好支持 innovation（创新）。其他选项不是该页问题。
questions.source: p.4: 'What types of banking applications would be best suited for agile development?'

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the slides' view of IT solutions and business value?
options: Technology should be viewed as a means of delivering business value, and ideally processes should determine IT systems
IT systems should always determine business processes, regardless of business value
IT solutions should only address technical problems, not operational problems
Business value is unrelated to IT solution delivery
questions.explanation: p.5 说 IT solutions（IT 解决方案）address business and operational problems（业务和运营问题）、improve efficiencies（提升效率）、enable new business initiatives（支持新业务举措）；technology should be viewed as means of delivering business value（交付业务价值的手段）；ideally, processes should determine IT systems（流程应决定 IT 系统），not the other way around（而不是反过来）。
questions.source: p.5: 'Technology should be viewed as means of delivering business value / processes should determine IT systems, not the other way around'

questions.question: Which statements about fulfilling business objectives are correct according to the slides?
options: Solutions implement banks' corporate strategies
Tactical concerns can draw attention away from strategic considerations
A solution delivery plan should balance strategic and tactical considerations
Management does not need to communicate key goals and objectives
questions.explanation: p.6 说 solutions implement banks' corporate strategies（公司战略）；tactical concerns（战术性关注点）often can draw attention away from strategic considerations（战略性考虑）；重要的是 create a solution delivery plan（解决方案交付计划）that balances strategic and tactical considerations；management must define and effectively communicate its key goals and objectives（关键目标和目的）。因此 D 错在否定沟通。
questions.source: p.6: 'Solutions implement banks corporate strategies / Tactical concerns can draw attention away from strategic considerations / balances strategic and tactical considerations'

questions.question: Who is the 30,000-foot view mainly for, and what does it emphasize?
options: Senior management and other stakeholders; it links solution initiatives with business goals and highlights interdependencies
Line managers and implementers; it specifies detailed design specifications
Vendors only; it defines contract penalties
Testers only; it lists all test cases
questions.explanation: p.7 说 The 30,000-foot view（3 万英尺视图）is why and what（为何与做什么），for senior management and other stakeholders（高层管理及其他利益相关者），solutions initiatives are linked with business goals（与业务目标关联），interdependencies are highlighted（依赖关系被突出）。detailed design specifications（详细设计规格）属于 p.10 的 2,000-foot view（2 千英尺视图）。
questions.source: p.7: 'The 30,000-foot view: why and what / For senior management and other stakeholders / linked with business goals / Interdependencies are highlighted'

questions.question: Which description best matches the 10,000-foot view in the slides?
options: It involves middle management, focuses on the golden path or main flow, and uses high-level process models
It is only for line managers and contains detailed use-case descriptions
It shows physical servers and network hardware configuration
It is a post-project review of what worked well
questions.explanation: p.8 说 The 10,000-foot view（1 万英尺视图）is what and how（做什么与如何做），involves middle management（中层管理），focus on the most likely process flow（最可能的流程），即 golden path（黄金路径）或 main flow（主流程）；high-level process models（高层流程模型）useful。detailed use-case descriptions（详细用例描述）属于 p.10；physical servers（物理服务器）是物理图；post-project review（项目后评审）是 p.27。
questions.source: p.8: 'The 10,000-foot view: what and how / Involves middle management / golden path or main flow / High level process models'

questions.question: In the fee billing main flow example, which step belongs to the Fee Management System?
options: Retrieve Remittance Fees
Retrieve Subscription Fees
Collect Fee Details
Retrieve Audit Conf. Fees
questions.explanation: p.9 的 fee billing process（费用计费流程）图中，Fee Management System（费用管理系统）负责 Collect Fee Details（收集费用明细）、Aggregate Fees（汇总费用）、Apply Bundling Adjustments（应用捆绑调整）、Generate Fee Reports（生成费用报告）。Retrieve Remittance Fees（获取汇款费用）属于 Core Banking System（核心银行系统）；Retrieve Subscription Fees（获取订阅费用）属于 Subscription Services System（订阅服务系统）；Retrieve Audit Conf. Fees（获取审计确认费用）属于 Customer Service System（客户服务系统）。
questions.source: p.9: diagram 'Fee Management System / Collect Fee Details / Aggregate Fees / Generate Fee Reports'

questions.question: Which tools are listed for capturing and communicating requirements at the 2,000-foot view?
options: Detailed business process models
Use-case descriptions
Design specifications
Physical network hardware diagrams
questions.explanation: p.10 说 2,000-foot view（2 千英尺视图）captures and communicates（捕获并沟通）常用 detailed business process models（详细业务流程模型）、use-case descriptions（用例描述）、design specifications（设计规格）。physical network hardware diagrams（物理网络硬件图）不是该页列出的工具，而更接近 p.11 的 physical diagram（物理图）概念。
questions.source: p.10: 'Detailed business process models / Use-case descriptions / Design specifications'

questions.question: Which user story snippet illustrates the condition for waiving monthly account service fees in the slides?
options: As a customer, I want monthly account service fees waived when current account assets are over $500,000
As a customer, I want all fees waived regardless of account assets
As a customer, I want monthly fees increased when assets are over $500,000
As a customer, I want fee reports generated by the vendor
questions.explanation: p.11 的 detailed user story（详细用户故事）示例写：As a customer, I want monthly account service fees waived（希望月度账户服务费被免除）when current account assets over $500,000（活期账户资产超过 50 万美元）。其他选项把条件、方向或主体改错。
questions.source: p.11: 'monthly account service fees waived / current account assets over $500,000'

questions.question: Why is defining solution scope and priorities critical in high-level delivery planning?
options: Without a clear scope, the delivery has no clear endpoint or success criteria
Because scope should never be communicated to stakeholders
Because total cost of ownership should be ignored
Because priorities are only relevant after deployment
questions.explanation: p.12 说 defining solution scope and priorities（定义解决方案范围和优先级）critical；without a clear scope（没有清晰范围），delivery has no clear endpoint or success criteria（没有明确终点或成功标准）；还需要 consensus（共识）并 clear communication（清晰沟通），并考虑 expected lifetime（预期寿命）和 total cost of ownership（总拥有成本）。
questions.source: p.12: 'Without a clear scope, the delivery has no clear endpoint or success criteria'

questions.question: Which of the following are key considerations in high-level delivery planning according to the slides?
options: What existing enterprise platforms can be leveraged to reduce cost and effort and improve quality
Which legacy systems should be avoided, if possible
What enterprise platforms not currently in place could be partially implemented as part of the solution delivery effort
Is the expectation to build or buy the system
Should the bank avoid all involvement in solution delivery
questions.explanation: p.13 列出关键考虑：利用 existing enterprise platforms（现有企业平台）降低成本/工作量并提升质量；avoid legacy systems（避免遗留系统）；部分实施尚未具备的 enterprise platforms（企业平台）；build or buy（自建或购买）；以及 bank intended level of involvement（银行预期参与程度）。E 与原文相反，slides 问的是参与程度，不是完全回避。
questions.source: p.13: 'What existing enterprise platforms can be leveraged / Which legacy systems should be avoided / build or buy / level of involvement'

questions.question: Which risks are listed under assessing and managing risks in solution delivery?
options: Scope creep
Technology risk from new, unproven technology
Vendor risk that the vendor does not deliver as promised
Cost control risk where delays or overruns exceed the budget
Guaranteed vendor delivery as promised
questions.explanation: p.14 列出 scope creep（范围蔓延）、technology（新技术/未经验证技术的风险）、vendor（供应商不按承诺交付）、project delivery（项目管理/实施不佳）和 cost control（延迟或超支导致预算被突破）。E 与 vendor risk（供应商风险）相反，不是 listed risk。
questions.source: p.14: 'Scope creep / Technology / Vendor / Cost control / Delays or overruns cause the budget to be exceeded'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the conflicting constraints listed under evaluating trade-offs?
options: Number of features
Time-to-market
Quality
Guaranteed zero cost
questions.explanation: p.15 说 evaluating trade-offs（评估权衡）是 balancing between conflicting constraints（平衡冲突约束），列出 number of features（功能数量）、time-to-market（上市时间）、quality（质量）、cost（成本）。Guaranteed zero cost（保证零成本）不是 listed constraint，也不现实。
questions.source: p.15: 'Number of features / Time-to-market / Quality / Cost'

questions.question: Which solution construction approaches are listed in the slides?
options: Buy
Build
Assemble
White-labeled / Software as a Service (SaaS)
Code and fix
questions.explanation: p.16 列出 solution construction approaches（解决方案构建方式）包括 Buy（购买）、Build（自建）、Assemble（组装）、White-labeled / Software as a Service (SaaS)（白标/软件即服务）。Code and fix（编码并修复）是 p.23 的 delivery approach（交付方式），不是该页 construction approach。
questions.source: p.16: 'Buy / Build / Assemble / White-labeled / Software as a Service (SaaS)'

questions.question: Which is a logistical challenge of using external and remote resources for implementation according to the slides?
options: Coordinating between time zones and cultures and having a lack of visibility of progress
Guaranteed lower quality because external resources are always less skilled
Elimination of all coordination costs
Automatic increase in stakeholder interest
questions.explanation: p.17 说 external and remote resources（外部与远程资源）often provides cost benefits（成本收益），但也 creates logistical challenges（后勤挑战）：coordinating between time zones and cultures（协调时区与文化）、lack of visibility of progress（缺乏进度可见性）。其他选项不是 slides 原意。
questions.source: p.17: 'Coordinating between time zones and cultures / Lack of visibility of progress'

questions.question: What is the correct solution conception flow shown in the slides?
options: High-level Needs Analysis → High-level Planning and Arch. Design → Feasibility Analysis → Approval to Move Forward → Solution Instantiation
High-level Planning and Arch. Design → High-level Needs Analysis → Approval to Move Forward → Feasibility Analysis → Solution Instantiation
Feasibility Analysis → High-level Needs Analysis → Approval to Move Forward → High-level Planning and Arch. Design → Solution Instantiation
Approval to Move Forward → High-level Needs Analysis → Feasibility Analysis → High-level Planning and Arch. Design → Solution Instantiation
questions.explanation: p.18 图显示 solution conception（解决方案构思）流程为 High-level Needs Analysis（高层需求分析）→ High-level Planning and Arch. Design（高层规划与架构设计）→ Feasibility Analysis（可行性分析）→ Approval to Move Forward（批准推进）→ Solution Instantiation（解决方案实例化）。其他顺序打乱。
questions.source: p.18: diagram 'High-level Needs Analysis / High-level Planning and Arch. Design / Feasibility Analysis / Approval to Move Forward / Solution Instantiation'

questions.question: What does high-level needs analysis articulate according to the slides?
options: What the solution will be, why it is valuable, and how it fits with the organization's business strategy
The exact code structure and database schema
The vendor's internal profit margin
The final test scripts and deployment checklist
questions.explanation: p.19 说 high-level needs analysis（高层需求分析）articulate（阐明）what the solution will be（解决方案将是什么）、why it is valuable（为何有价值）、how it fits with the organization's business strategy（如何契合组织业务战略）。其他选项属于更后期或外部内容。
questions.source: p.19: 'What the solution will be / Why it is valuable / How it fits with the organization's business strategy'

questions.question: The slides state that high-level planning and design should define the overall solution-delivery timeline and budget.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.20 说 high-level planning and design（高层规划与设计）要给出 high-level sketch（高层草图）of how the solution could be constructed，考虑 current environment and capabilities（当前环境与能力），review building blocks and systems（构建块与系统）available in the market，并 define overall solution-delivery timeline and budget（整体交付时间线和预算）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.20: 'Define overall solution-delivery timeline and budget'

questions.question: Which are examples of critical limitations that feasibility analysis reviews in the existing environment?
options: Interfaces are not available to access systems
Interfaces are available but too expensive to utilize
Access to a system is dependent on it being upgraded
Cooperation of a third party is required, such as a vendor or separate business division
All interfaces are always free and immediately available
questions.explanation: p.21 说 feasibility analysis（可行性分析）identifies and validates assumptions（识别并验证假设），并审查 existing environment（现有环境）是否存在 critical limitations（关键限制），例如 interfaces（接口）不可用、接口可用但 too expensive to utilize（使用成本过高）、access dependent on upgrade（访问依赖系统升级）、cooperation of a third party（第三方合作）required。E 与原文相反。
questions.source: p.21: 'Interfaces are not available / too expensive to utilize / dependent on it being upgraded / Cooperation of a third party is required'

questions.question: Which statement about approval to move forward is correct according to the slides?
options: Signing a letter of intent (LOI) may be sufficient to get work started
Approval is always decided only by the CIO and a senior business manager, never by committee
All terms and conditions must always be fully agreed before solution instantiation begins
Approval never leads to negotiations with external vendors
questions.explanation: p.22 说 approval to move forward（批准推进）process varies by organization（因组织而异），可能由 CIO and a senior business manager（首席信息官和高级业务经理）决定，也可能由 committee（委员会）决定；approval gives way to negotiations with external vendors（外部供应商谈判）；terms and conditions（条款和条件）可能持续到 instantiation phase（实例化阶段）；signing a letter of intent (LOI)（签署意向书）may be sufficient to get work started（可能足以启动工作）。
questions.source: p.22: 'Signing a letter of intent (LOI) may be sufficient to get work started'

questions.question: Which statement best describes the waterfall delivery approach in the slides?
options: Sequential and easily tracked, but slow to deliver visible results, with misunderstandings showing up late
Progress is visible throughout and ideas can be adapted during delivery
It incurs no delays for planning and requirements gathering
It always eliminates structural flaws by skipping planning
questions.explanation: p.23 说 waterfall（瀑布式）是 sequential and easily tracked（顺序化且易于跟踪），但 slow to deliver visible results（难以快速交付可见成果），misunderstandings show up late in the delivery process（误解在交付后期才暴露）。B 描述 iterative（迭代式）；C、D 描述 code and fix（编码并修复）的某些特点且表述错误。
questions.source: p.23: 'Waterfall / Sequential and easily tracked / Slow to deliver visible results / Misunderstandings show up late'

questions.question: Which is a drawback of the iterative delivery approach listed in the slides?
options: It is less familiar to many project teams and managers and more difficult to estimate total project duration
Progress is not visible throughout the project
Ideas cannot be adapted during the delivery process
It is sequential and easily tracked
questions.explanation: p.23 说 iterative（迭代式）的优点是 progress is visible throughout（全程可见）、ideas can be adapted（想法可调整）；缺点是 less familiar to many project teams and managers（许多项目团队和管理者不熟悉）以及 more difficult to estimate total project duration（更难估算总项目周期）。A 正确概括了缺点；B、C 与优点相反；D 是 waterfall（瀑布式）的特点。
questions.source: p.23: 'Less familiar to many project teams and managers / More difficult to estimate total project duration'

questions.question: The slides state that code and fix does not incur delays for planning and requirements gathering, but lack of planning can lead to major structural flaws.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.23 说 code and fix（编码并修复）does not incur delays for planning and requirements gathering（不会因计划和需求收集而延迟），但 lack of planning can lead to major structural flaws（缺乏计划可能导致重大结构性缺陷）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.23: 'Does not incur delays for planning and requirements gathering / Lack of planning can lead to major structural flaws'

questions.question: In the solution instantiation diagram, which stage directly follows Testing?
options: Deployment
Project Planning
Requirements Analysis
Architecture Design
questions.explanation: p.24 的 solution instantiation（解决方案实例化）图顺序为 Project Planning（项目规划）→ Requirements Analysis（需求分析）与 Architecture Design（架构设计）→ Implementation（实施）→ Testing（测试）→ Deployment（部署）→ Support（支持）与 Review（评审）。Testing 之后直接是 Deployment。
questions.source: p.24: diagram 'Testing' followed by 'Deployment'

questions.question: Which statement about requirements analysis is correct according to the slides?
options: Inadequate requirements are the second most significant contributing factor to project failure
Requirements analysis is never important compared with deployment
Bullet-point functional descriptions are the strongest form of requirements documentation
Nonfunctional aspects such as performance and compliance are not critical
questions.explanation: p.25 说 requirements analysis（需求分析）often the most important part of the project（通常是项目最重要部分）；inadequate requirements（不充分需求）是 the second most significant contributing factor to project failure（项目失败第二大贡献因素）；good documentation（良好文档）是 detailed process models and/or use cases（详细流程模型/用例）；weak（弱）的是 bullet-point functional descriptions（要点式功能描述，又称 user wish lists（用户愿望清单））；还要 capture nonfunctional aspects（非功能方面），例如 performance（性能）和 compliance（合规）。
questions.source: p.25: 'Inadequate requirements are the second most significant contributing factor to project failure'

questions.question: Which are good forms of requirements documentation according to the slides?
options: Detailed process models
Use cases
Bullet-point functional descriptions (user wish lists)
Detailed design specifications for every future change
questions.explanation: p.25 说 Good（良好）requirements documentation（需求文档）是 detailed process models（详细流程模型）and/or use cases（用例）；Weak（弱）的是 bullet-point functional descriptions（要点式功能描述，a.k.a. user wish lists（又称用户愿望清单））。D 不是该页所列 good documentation 形式。
questions.source: p.25: 'Good: detailed process models and/or use cases / Weak: bullet-point functional descriptions'

questions.question: Why is testing especially important for financial services solutions according to the slides?
options: Failures in production can lead to significant financial losses
Testing eliminates the need for requirements analysis
Testing is only useful for code and fix projects
Testing replaces deployment and support
questions.explanation: p.26 说 testing（测试）对 financial services solutions（金融服务解决方案）important，因为 failures in production（生产环境失败）can lead to significant financial losses（重大财务损失）。testing 不能替代 requirements analysis（需求分析）、deployment（部署）或 support（支持）。
questions.source: p.26: 'Failures in production can lead to significant financial losses'

questions.question: The slides state that deployment and support should be considered during requirements and design, and a solution that is hard to administer and maintain is not a successful one.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.26 说 Deployment and support（部署与支持）should be considered during requirements and design（应在需求与设计阶段考虑）；A solution that is hard to administer and maintain（难以管理和维护的解决方案）is not a successful one（不是成功方案）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.26: 'Deployment and support / Should be considered during requirements and design / hard to administer and maintain is not a successful one'

questions.question: What should post-project reviews identify according to the slides?
options: What worked well and should be repeated in future delivery efforts
What did not work well and should be done differently in future delivery efforts
What should have been done but was not
Ways to ignore previous mistakes so they are not discussed
questions.explanation: p.27 说 post-project reviews（项目后评审）important to identify what worked well and should be repeated（哪些做得好应重复）、what did not work well and should be done differently（哪些不好应改变）、what should have been done but was not（哪些本应做却未做）；这些应考虑进 future solutions（未来解决方案）并 help avoid repeating previous mistakes（帮助避免重复此前错误）。D 与原文相反。
questions.source: p.27: 'What worked well / What did not work well / What should have been done but was not'

questions.question: The slides state that successful solutions begin by having everyone understand the big picture.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.28 原文写 Successful solutions begin by having everyone understand the big picture（成功解决方案始于让每个人理解全局）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.28: 'Successful solutions begin by having everyone understand the big picture'

questions.question: Which responsibilities are associated with the solution champion in the slides?
options: Convince key stakeholders to support the solution delivery
Maintain the delivery team's motivation and stakeholders' interests throughout the project
Drive the project to closure and acceptance
Assume that the last 10% of the project is always the easiest
questions.explanation: p.29 说 critical to have a champion（拥护者/推动者）for the solution，often project manager or business sponsor（项目经理或业务发起人）；must convince key stakeholders（关键利益相关者）to support；maintains delivery team's motivation（团队积极性）and stakeholders' interests（利益相关者兴趣）；drive the project to closure and acceptance（推动收尾与验收）；the last 10% is usually the hardest（最后 10% 通常最难）。D 与原文相反。
questions.source: p.29: 'Convince key stakeholders / Maintains delivery team motivation / Drive the project to closure and acceptance / last 10% is usually the hardest'

questions.question: The slides suggest that for some institutions increasing investment in technology will not yield material benefits.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.2 明确说 For some, increasing investment in technology will not yield material benefits（对某些机构而言，增加技术投资不会带来实质性收益）；For others, the level of investment in technology will determine their relative success（对另一些机构，技术投资水平决定相对成功）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.2: 'For some, increasing investment in technology will not yield material benefits'

questions.question: Which technology firms do the slides cite as showing how technology can be used to create and upset entire industries?
options: Google and Uber
Amazon and Visa
SWIFT and IBM
Oracle and SAP
questions.explanation: p.3 说 Google and Uber（谷歌与优步）have shown how technology can be used create and upset entire industries（创造并颠覆整个行业）。Amazon 的例子在该页用于说明能每分钟多次发布生产软件变更；其他公司组合未在该页这样引用。
questions.source: p.3: 'Google and Uber have shown how technology can be used create and upset entire industries'

questions.question: The slides state that ideally processes should determine IT systems, not the other way around.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.5 原文写 Ideally, processes should determine IT systems, not the other way around（理想情况下，应由流程决定 IT 系统，而不是反过来）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.5: 'Ideally, processes should determine IT systems, not the other way around'

questions.question: What warning about tactical concerns is given in the slides?
options: Tactical concerns can draw attention away from strategic considerations
Tactical concerns always improve strategic alignment
Strategic considerations should be ignored during delivery planning
Tactical concerns eliminate the need to communicate goals
questions.explanation: p.6 说 Often tactical concerns（战术性关注点）can draw attention away from strategic considerations（战略性考虑），因此 solution delivery plan（解决方案交付计划）应 balance strategic and tactical considerations（平衡战略与战术考虑）。其他选项与原文相反。
questions.source: p.6: 'Often tactical concerns can draw attention away from strategic considerations'

questions.question: What does the 30,000-foot view highlight among solution initiatives?
options: Interdependencies and their linkage with business goals
Detailed database schemas and code libraries
Individual test scripts and deployment checklists
Vendor contract penalty clauses
questions.explanation: p.7 说 30,000-foot view（3 万英尺视图）强调 solution initiatives（解决方案举措）linked with business goals（与业务目标关联），并且 interdependencies（相互依赖关系）are highlighted（被突出）。详细数据库模式、测试脚本和合同罚则不是该层视图内容。
questions.source: p.7: 'Solutions initiatives are linked with business goals / Interdependencies are highlighted'

questions.question: What is solution conception described as in the slides?
options: A filtering mechanism for business ideas that helps ensure projects moving to instantiation will be successful
A replacement for all requirements analysis after deployment
A guarantee that every idea will be approved
A method for skipping feasibility analysis
questions.explanation: p.18 说 solution conception（解决方案构思）is a filtering mechanism for business ideas（业务想法的过滤机制），helps ensure that projects that move forward to the instantiation phase（进入实例化阶段的项目）will be successful。它不是部署后的需求分析替代，也不保证所有想法获批或跳过 feasibility analysis（可行性分析）。
questions.source: p.18: 'Is a filtering mechanism for business ideas / Helps ensure that projects that move forward to the instantiation phase will be successful'

questions.question: What does the slides say about running a proof of concept exercise in feasibility analysis?
options: It is often prudent to run a proof of concept exercise to demonstrate feasibility
It should never be used because it replaces all requirements analysis
It is only useful after deployment
It guarantees approval by the committee
questions.explanation: p.21 说 It is often prudent to run a proof of concept exercise（运行概念验证练习）to demonstrate feasibility（证明可行性）。它不替代 requirements analysis（需求分析），不是部署后使用，也不保证 committee（委员会）批准。
questions.source: p.21: 'It is often prudent to run a proof of concept exercise to demonstrate feasibility'

questions.question: According to the slides, maintaining IT systems consumes approximately what proportion of banks' IT spending?
options: One-quarter
One-half
Three-quarters
All of it
questions.explanation: p.2 明确估计 the cost of maintaining IT systems（维护 IT 系统的成本）consumes three-quarters of banks' IT spending（占银行 IT 支出的四分之三）。one-quarter（四分之一）和 one-half（一半）低估；all of it（全部）夸大。
questions.source: p.2: 'three-quarters of banks IT spending'

questions.question: Which statements about banks' existing infrastructure and IT priorities are correct according to the slides?
options: Banks' hardware and software environments are large and complex
Existing infrastructure and systems dominate the IT landscape of banks
Keeping the lights on often takes priority over implementation of new systems
Maintaining IT systems is estimated to consume three-quarters of banks' IT spending
questions.explanation: p.2 说硬件和软件环境 large and complex（庞大复杂）；existing infrastructure and systems（现有基础设施和系统）dominate（主导）IT landscape；keeping the lights on（维持系统运行）often takes priority over new systems；并估计维护成本占 banks' IT spending（银行 IT 支出）three-quarters（四分之三）。四项都正确。
questions.source: p.2: 'large and complex / dominate the IT landscape / Keeping the lights on / three-quarters of banks IT spending'

questions.question: Which question is NOT listed in the Royal Bank of Scotland system operation case study on p.3?
options: What steps can banks take to minimize the likelihood of system failures besides implementing IT system resiliency?
Why might the £750 million investment not have prevented the 2015 incident?
Is minimizing IT environment changes a practical strategy for limiting risks?
What is the exact number of employees in every bank's IT helpdesk?
questions.explanation: p.3 的 case study 问题包括：除 resiliency（弹性）外如何降低系统故障可能性、如何降低故障影响、为何 £750 million investment（7.5 亿英镑投资）未阻止 2015 incident（事件）、minimizing IT environment changes（最小化 IT 环境变更）是否实际、以及 other internal costs（其他内部成本）。没有问每家银行 IT helpdesk（服务台）的精确员工数。
questions.source: p.3: 'System Operation Woes at Royal Bank of Scotland / Questions'

questions.question: Which characteristics are associated with IBM-PC compatible compute resources in the slides?
options: Low cost, commodity hardware
Flexible and open
Used for most software applications
Commonly used for core-banking mainframe workloads
questions.explanation: p.5 说 IBM-PC compatible（IBM-PC 兼容）是 low cost, commodity hardware（低成本商品化硬件）、flexible and open（灵活开放）、used for most software applications（用于大多数软件应用）。core-banking（核心银行）mainframe workloads（大型机工作负载）对应 mainframes，不是 IBM-PC compatible。
questions.source: p.5: 'IBM-PC compatible / Low cost, commodity hardware / Flexible and open / Used for most software applications'

questions.question: The slides describe mini-computers such as IBM AS/400 as having limited use.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.5 在 Mini-computers（小型机）例如 IBM AS/400 下写 Limited use（用途有限）。因此该判断正确。
questions.source: p.5: 'Mini-computers (e.g. IBM AS/400) / Limited use'

questions.question: Which statement best describes mainframes according to the slides?
options: Commonly used for core-banking applications, reliable and supporting high volumes, but costly
Low-cost commodity hardware used for most software applications
A collection of disk drives that appears as a single shared file system
The main user interface for thin-client applications
questions.explanation: p.5 说 Mainframes（大型机）commonly used for core-banking applications（核心银行应用），reliable and support high volumes（可靠并支持高容量），but costly（但成本高）。B 是 IBM-PC compatible；C 是 NAS；D 是 web browsers。
questions.source: p.5: 'Mainframes / Commonly used for core-banking applications / Reliable and support high volumes, but costly'

questions.question: What is Network Attached Storage (NAS) according to the slides?
options: A collection of disk drives that appear as a single shared file system
A coordinated group of devices that manage multiple disks
A low-level instruction set baked into hardware
A component that distributes network requests across multiple servers
questions.explanation: p.6 定义 NAS（网络附加存储）为 a collection of disk drives that appear as a single shared file system（一组磁盘驱动器，表现为单一共享文件系统）。B 是 SAN（存储区域网络）；C 是 firmware（固件）；D 是 load balancer（负载均衡器）。
questions.source: p.6: 'Network Attached Storage (NAS) – a collection of disk drives that appear as a single shared file system'

questions.question: What is a Storage Area Network (SAN) according to the slides?
options: A coordinated group of devices that manage multiple disks
A single shared file system made of disk drives
A tape system used only to archive information
The main user interface for thin-client applications
questions.explanation: p.6 定义 SAN（存储区域网络）为 a coordinated group of devices that manage multiple disks（协调管理多个磁盘的一组设备）。A 描述的是 NAS；C 只描述 tape backup 的一部分；D 是 web browser。
questions.source: p.6: 'Storage Area Networks (SANs) – a coordinated group of devices that manage multiple disks'

questions.question: What are tape backup systems used for according to the slides?
options: To back up data that is stored on hard disks
To archive information
To manage multiple virtual servers' interactions with hardware
To distribute network requests across multiple servers
questions.explanation: p.6 说 tape backup systems（磁带备份系统）used to back up data stored on hard disks（备份硬盘上的数据）and to archive information（归档信息）。C 是 hypervisor（管理程序）；D 是 load balancer（负载均衡器）。
questions.source: p.6: 'Tape backup systems – used to back up data that is stored on hard disks and to archive information'

questions.question: What is firmware according to the slides?
options: Low-level instructions baked into computer hardware and used to load the operating system
A collection of disk drives that appears as a shared file system
The main user interface for thin-client applications
A coordinated group of devices that manage multiple disks
questions.explanation: p.7 定义 firmware（固件）为 the low-level instructions that are baked into computer hardware（固化在计算机硬件中的低级指令）and used to load the operating system（用于加载操作系统），stored on persistent programmable memory chips on circuit boards（存储在电路板上的持久可编程存储芯片）。
questions.source: p.7: 'The low-level instructions that are baked into computer hardware and used to load the operating system'

questions.question: What is the role of a hypervisor according to the slides?
options: It is the operating system that manages and coordinates different virtual servers' interactions with the hardware
It stores data on tape backup systems
It receives HTTP requests and returns HTML content
It restricts the flow of network traffic between devices
questions.explanation: p.8 说 hypervisor（管理程序/虚拟机监视器）is the operating system that manages and coordinates the different virtual servers' interactions with the hardware（管理和协调不同虚拟服务器与硬件交互的操作系统）。B 是 tape backup；C 是 web server；D 是 firewall。
questions.source: p.8: 'The hypervisor is the operating system that manages and coordinates the different virtual servers interactions with the hardware'

questions.question: The slides state that each virtual server is an operating system that shares the physical server's resources with other operating system instances running on the same physical server.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.8 原文写 Each virtual server is an operating system（每个虚拟服务器是一个操作系统）that shares the physical server's resources（共享物理服务器资源）with other operating system instances running on the same physical server（同一物理服务器上的其他操作系统实例）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.8: 'Each virtual server is an operating system that shares the physical server's resources'

questions.question: The p.9 diagram indicates that each virtual machine running within the hypervisor is the equivalent of a standalone server operating system.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.9 图下文字明确写 Each virtual machine running within the hypervisor is the equivalent of a standalone server operating system（在管理程序内运行的每个虚拟机等同于一个独立服务器操作系统）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.9: 'Each virtual machine running within the hypervisor is the equivalent of a standalone server operating system'

questions.question: Which resources does an operating system manage access to according to the slides?
options: Microprocessor and memory
Disk drives
Displays
Network interfaces
questions.explanation: p.10 说 operating systems（操作系统）manages software applications' access to the microprocessor, memory, disk drives, displays, and network interfaces（管理软件应用对微处理器、内存、磁盘驱动器、显示器和网络接口的访问）。四项都在原文列表中。
questions.source: p.10: 'Manages software applications access to the microprocessor, memory, disk drives, displays, and network interfaces'

questions.question: Which operating system pairing is correct according to the slides?
options: Linux and Microsoft Windows on commodity server and workstation hardware; z/OS on mainframe hardware
z/OS on commodity server hardware; Linux on mainframe hardware only
Microsoft Windows only on mainframes; Linux only on tape backup systems
IBM AS/400 on web browsers; z/OS on NAS appliances
questions.explanation: p.10 说 common operating systems（常见操作系统）包括 Linux and Microsoft Windows（Linux 与微软 Windows）on commodity server and workstation hardware（商品化服务器和工作站硬件），以及 z/OS on mainframe hardware（大型机硬件）。其他配对与原文不符。
questions.source: p.10: 'Linux and Microsoft Windows on commodity server and workstation hardware / z/OS on mainframe hardware'

questions.question: Which statements about drivers are correct according to the slides?
options: Drivers provide a common way for the operating system to access network interfaces
Drivers provide access to peripherals such as printers and scanners
Some drivers may be loaded directly by software applications to access databases and middleware components
Drivers are the main user interface for thin-client applications
questions.explanation: p.11 说 drivers（驱动程序）provide a common way for the OS（操作系统）to access network interfaces（网络接口）、peripherals（外围设备，如 printers and scanners（打印机和扫描仪））、other resources；some drivers may be loaded directly by software applications（软件应用直接加载）to access databases（数据库）和 middleware components（中间件组件）。D 是 web browsers 的描述。
questions.source: p.11: 'Provide a common way for the operating system to access network interfaces / peripherals / Some drivers may be loaded directly by software applications'

questions.question: Which statements about relational databases (RDBs) are correct according to the slides?
options: They are the primary means by which software applications store and manipulate information
Commercial and open-source RDBs are available
Storing application data in an RDB provides centralized persistent storage
RDBs can be used for information management and reporting purposes
questions.explanation: p.12 说 Relational databases (RDBs)（关系型数据库）是软件应用 store and manipulate information（存储和操作信息）的 primary means（主要手段）；commercial and open-source（商业和开源）RDBs 可用；RDB 存储提供 centralized persistent storage（集中持久化存储）；也可用于 information management and reporting（信息管理与报表）。四项均正确。
questions.source: p.12: 'Relational databases (RDBs) / centralized persistent storage / information management and reporting purposes'

questions.question: Where is business logic implemented in tiered software applications according to the slides?
options: Application servers
Tape backup systems
Firewalls
Web browsers only
questions.explanation: p.13 说 Application servers（应用服务器）是 where business logic is implemented in tiered software applications（分层软件应用中实现业务逻辑的地方）；它们也是 runtime engines（运行时引擎）execute programming language instructions（执行编程语言指令）。
questions.source: p.13: 'Application servers / Where business logic is implemented in tiered software applications'

questions.question: Why does centralizing business logic in the application server reduce maintenance effort according to the slides?
options: It centralizes where the business logic is kept rather than implementing it in the database or application display logic
It eliminates the need for any operating system
It automatically encrypts all network traffic
It replaces all external interfaces with APIs
questions.explanation: p.13 说 storing the business logic in the application server centralizes where it is kept（集中保存业务逻辑），opposed to implementing in the database or the application display logic（而不是在数据库或应用显示逻辑中实现），thus reduces maintenance effort（减少维护工作）。其他选项不是该页原因。
questions.source: p.13: 'Centralizes where it is kept / Opposed to implementing in the database or the application display logic / Reduces maintenance effort'

questions.question: Which functions are associated with web servers in the slides?
options: Receive HTTP requests and return HTML content
Deliver static, predefined web page content
Deliver dynamic, programmatically generated content
Create encrypted communication sessions between networks
questions.explanation: p.14 说 web servers（Web 服务器）receive HTTP requests（接收 HTTP 请求）and return HTML content（返回 HTML 内容），deliver static, predefined web page content（静态预定义网页内容）and dynamic, programmatically generated content（动态程序生成内容）。D 是 VPN（虚拟专用网络）的功能。
questions.source: p.14: 'Receive HTTP requests and return HTML content / static, predefined web page content / dynamic, programmatically generated content'

questions.question: What do scripts running on the web server often do according to the slides?
options: Make requests to an application server to retrieve information or perform calculations
Manage virtual servers' interactions with hardware
Restrict network traffic between devices
Back up hard disk data to tape
questions.explanation: p.14 说 scripts（脚本）running on the web server（在 Web 服务器上运行）provide functions for dynamically generating HTML（动态生成 HTML），其 output dependent on parameters received as part of the request（输出取决于请求参数），并且 scripts will often make requests to an application server（常向应用服务器发起请求）to retrieve information or perform calculations（获取信息或执行计算）。
questions.source: p.14: 'Scripts will often make requests to an application server to retrieve information or perform calculations'

questions.question: How does the slides describe middleware?
options: The communication components that glue all the other components together
The low-level instructions baked into hardware
A collection of disk drives that appears as a shared file system
The main user interface for thin-client applications
questions.explanation: p.15 定义 middleware（中间件）为 the communication components that glue all the other components together（把所有其他组件粘合起来的通信组件）。B 是 firmware；C 是 NAS；D 是 web browser。
questions.source: p.15: 'The communication components that glue all the other components together'

questions.question: Which features are associated with Java Message Service (JMS) in the slides?
options: Message queuing
Point-to-point delivery
Publish-subscribe delivery
Creating encrypted VPN sessions
questions.explanation: p.15 说 Java Message Service (JMS)（Java 消息服务）provides more advanced features（更高级功能）：message queuing（消息队列）、point-to-point and publish-subscribe delivery（点对点与发布-订阅交付）。D 是 VPN 的功能。
questions.source: p.15: 'Java Message Service (JMS) / message queuing / point-to-point and publish-subscribe delivery'

questions.question: The slides state that web browsers are the main user interface for thin-client applications, and that HTML version five enabled more complex applications to be developed and run in web browsers.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.16 说 Web browsers（Web 浏览器）are the main user interface for thin-client applications（瘦客户端应用的主要用户界面）；HTML version five（HTML5）enabled more complex applications（支持更复杂应用）to be developed and run in web browsers。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.16: 'The main user interface for thin-client applications / HTML version five enabled more complex applications'

questions.question: Which risks are associated with external interfaces and APIs according to the slides?
options: They add another layer of complexity and introduce additional change-related risk
The behavior of third-party interfaces may change, causing software applications to break or behave differently
A vendor or third party may stop supporting an interface version currently being used by an application
They eliminate all dependencies on third-party service providers
questions.explanation: p.17 说 external interfaces and APIs（外部接口和 API）add another layer of complexity（增加一层复杂性）and introduce additional change-related risk（引入额外变更相关风险）；third-party interfaces（第三方接口）behavior may change（行为可能变化），causing applications to break or behave differently（导致应用故障或行为不同）；vendor or third party may stop supporting an interface version（供应商或第三方可能停止支持某接口版本）。D 与原文相反。
questions.source: p.17: 'Another layer of complexity / behavior of third-party interfaces may change / vendor or third party may stop supporting an interface version'

questions.question: Which network communication component restricts the flow of network traffic between devices connected to the network?
options: Firewall
Router
Load balancer
VPN
questions.explanation: p.18 说 firewalls（防火墙）restrict the flow of network traffic（限制网络流量）between devices connected to the network。Router（路由器）links LANs and routes traffic（连接局域网并路由流量）；load balancer（负载均衡器）distributes network requests（分发网络请求）；VPN（虚拟专用网络）creates encrypted communication sessions（创建加密通信会话）。
questions.source: p.18: 'Firewalls – restrict the flow of network traffic between devices connected to the network'

questions.question: What do Automated Response Units (ARUs) do according to the slides?
options: Handle customers' service requests in place of or prior to interactions with agents
Link together LANs and route network traffic between them
Automatically dial phone numbers and route connected calls to agents
Create encrypted communication sessions between computers or networks
questions.explanation: p.19 说 Automated response units (ARUs)（自动响应单元）handle customers' service requests（处理客户服务请求）in place of or prior to interactions with agents（代替或先于与坐席互动）。B 是 router；C 是 predictive dialer；D 是 VPN。
questions.source: p.19: 'Automated response units (ARUs) – handle customers service requests in place of or prior to interactions with agents'

questions.question: What does a predictive dialer do according to the slides?
options: Automatically dials phone numbers and, if a connection is made, routes the call to an agent
Restricts the flow of network traffic between devices
Receives HTTP requests and returns HTML content
Manages multiple virtual servers' interactions with hardware
questions.explanation: p.19 说 predictive dialer（预测式拨号器）automatically dials phone numbers（自动拨打电话号码）；if a connection is made（若接通），will route the call to an agent（将呼叫路由给坐席）。其他选项分别是 firewall、web server、hypervisor。
questions.source: p.19: 'Predictive dialer – automatically dials phone numbers; if a connection is made, will route the call to an agent'

questions.question: The slides state that leased lines provide dedicated links between different locations, and MPLS networks provide connectivity between multiple sites.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.20 说 Leased lines（租用线路）provide dedicated links between different locations（不同地点之间的专用链路）；Multiprotocol label switching (MPLS) networks（多协议标签交换网络）provide connectivity between multiple sites（多站点连接）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.20: 'Leased lines provide dedicated links between different locations / MPLS networks provide connectivity between multiple sites'

questions.question: Which areas does the operational framework address according to the slides?
options: Competence, control, and consistency
Capacity and cost
Agility and customer focus
Guaranteed elimination of all operational risk
questions.explanation: p.22 说 operational framework（运营框架）aligns IT capabilities and services（IT 能力与服务）with overall business strategy（整体业务战略），addresses competence, control, consistency, capacity, cost, agility, and customer focus（能力、控制、一致性、容量、成本、敏捷性和客户关注）。它要求评估 likelihood and impact of operational risks（运营风险的可能性与影响）并排序，而不是保证消除所有风险。
questions.source: p.22: 'Addresses competence, control, consistency, capacity, cost, agility, and customer focus'

questions.question: What should be done with operational risks under the operational framework according to the slides?
options: Evaluate their likelihood and impact, then prioritize accordingly
Ignore them if they are difficult to measure
Eliminate all of them before any system is deployed
Delegate all of them to external vendors
questions.explanation: p.22 说 The likelihood and impact of operational risks（运营风险的可能性和影响）should be evaluated（应被评估），and then prioritized accordingly（并据此排序）。slides 没有说忽略、部署前全部消除或全部外包。
questions.source: p.22: 'The likelihood and impact of operational risks should be evaluated, and then prioritized accordingly'

questions.question: What does IT asset management involve according to the slides?
options: Tracking what hardware is connected to the network and what software is running on that hardware
Evaluating changes' potential effects and controlling their implementation
Restricting network traffic between devices
Automatically dialing phone numbers and routing calls
questions.explanation: p.24 说 IT Asset management（IT 资产管理）是 tracking what hardware is connected to the network and what software is running on that hardware（跟踪网络连接的硬件及其上运行的软件）。B 是 IT environment change management（IT 环境变更管理）；C 是 firewall；D 是 predictive dialer。
questions.source: p.24: 'IT Asset management – tracking what hardware is connected to the network and what software is running on that hardware'

questions.question: What is IT environment change management according to the slides?
options: Evaluating changes' potential effects and controlling their implementation
Tracking hardware connected to the network and software running on it
Creating encrypted communication sessions between computers
Handling customer service requests before agents
questions.explanation: p.24 说 IT environment change management（IT 环境变更管理）is evaluating changes' potential effects（评估变更潜在影响）and controlling their implementation（控制其实现）。B 是 IT asset management；C 是 VPN；D 是 ARU。
questions.source: p.24: 'IT environment change management – evaluating changes potential effects and controlling their implementation'

questions.question: The slides state that system updates and upgrades are critical for information security but can cause working systems to break.
options: 正确
错误
questions.explanation: p.24 说 System updates and upgrades（系统更新与升级）are critical for information security（对信息安全至关重要），but can cause working systems to break（但可能导致正在运行的系统故障）。因此判断正确。
questions.source: p.24: 'System updates and upgrades - critical for information security, but can cause working systems to break'

questions.question: Which matching of resilience terms is correct according to the slides?
